_doc: The turn profile: every timing knob of a live exchange in one place. Read live (no restarts) by the arm daemon, sim/chain.py, the studio (Run TURN, Charge+play) and the game's simple duel. Edit here or in the studio's Turn profile panel. Scale > 1 plays faster than the moves were tuned (1.5 = 50% faster); the servos are the limit, watch for 'OVER CAP' in the compile log.

_help.scale: playback speed of the moves: 1 = as tuned, 1.5 = 50% faster, 0.5 = half speed
_help.beats_per_pass: beats played per charge-in: 1 = back and forth every beat, 3 = a whole turn in one fluid pass
_help.overlap: true: the arms start their moves the instant the charge-in is sent (they swing during the ride); false: wait until the carriages arrive
_help.salute: both arms salute after arriving, before the moves (only when overlap is false)
_help.apart_after: back the carriages out to the apart stop after the pass
_help.pause_before_charge: seconds of stillness at the apart stop before the charge-in
_help.charge_feed: gantry feed for the charge-in, mm/min (controller max 24000)
_help.apart_feed: gantry feed for backing out, mm/min
_help.settle: seconds the daemon waits after easing into a move's first key before the trajectory clock starts
_help.ease_speed: deg/s for the ease from rest into the first key
_help.hold_end: seconds the arms hold their final pose after the moves before returning to rest
_help.return_speed: deg/s for the return to rest after the hold (the return is not part of the move)
_help.beat: chain compiler: seconds per beat (the move library was tuned at 1.4)
_help.impact: chain compiler: seconds into a beat where an attack lands
_help.guard: chain compiler: seconds into a beat where a block is in place
_help.return_t: chain compiler: seconds an attack takes to come back along its strike line before the next connector
_help.force_limit: per-joint servo load (0-1000) above which a strike on its way in is cut short; the daemon reports each play's peak load per joint in its status line, so set this from real numbers. A full-speed chop's own swing reads ~620 on the wrist/elbow; 0 = off
_help.force_ticks: how many consecutive 50 Hz ticks the load must stay over the limit before it counts (debounce)
_help.force_joints: which servos the force watch reads
_help.force_action: what a strike does when it meets the force limit: 'limp' = drop torque, stop the other arm, and wait for a human to reset it (the game pauses and asks); 'reverse' = end the forward sequence and back out along the strike line
